userStories.notes:
This is the integration story that wires everything together. All tool stories (MEM-003, W01) and storage (TSK-S) must be done first. After this story, the agent has a complete memory tool suite and clean production code.

CRITICAL DESIGN INSIGHT (see docs/cua-context-management.md): The CUA agent's context is a narrow sliding window. ImageRetentionCallback keeps only the last N screenshot triplets (reasoning + computer_call + computer_call_output), and OpenAI's truncation:auto drops the rest. By turn 100, only ~20 items survive out of ~300+. This has two key implications:

1. TASK_MEMORY.md MUST be injected into the `instructions` parameter (not as a tool result), because PromptInstructionsCallback prepends it on EVERY turn — it's the only content guaranteed to never be truncated. This is the primary cross-session knowledge transfer mechanism.

2. function_call_output items (memory_search/memory_get results) are ephemeral — they get truncated by the API like everything else. The agent only benefits from search results in the turn they're retrieved. Don't rely on the agent choosing to search; the most important memory goes in instructions.

userStories.notes:
Uses the same planner model (gpt-4.1-mini) that the nudge (US-MEM-004) will eventually use when upgraded. See docs/memory-system.md for compaction design.

Two-phase compaction:
1. compact_task_memory: session-NNN.md + existing TASK_MEMORY.md → compacted TASK_MEMORY.md (task-specific)
2. compact_global_memory: compacted TASK_MEMORY.md + existing MEMORY.md → compacted MEMORY.md (cross-task patterns)

The naive append consolidation in agenthle_agent.py (post-run block, lines ~203-237) serves as the interim mechanism and becomes the fallback if LLM compaction fails. This ensures data is never lost even if the compaction model is unavailable.

WARNING — Naive append causes unbounded growth: The current post-run block appends the FULL session log verbatim to both TASK_MEMORY.md and MEMORY.md after every run. After 5+ runs, both files become bloated with redundant observations, wasting context tokens when injected into instructions. LLM compaction MUST deduplicate, compress, and resolve contradictions — not just summarize. Each compacted output should be strictly shorter than (existing content + new session log).

userStories.notes:
Pure infrastructure story — no agent behavior changes, no new tools. The agent sees the same memory_search interface; only the backend changes from O(n) file scanning to indexed FTS5 queries.

Key design decisions:
1. Markdown files remain source of truth. SQLite is a derived index that can be rebuilt from scratch.
2. The embedding_cache table is created but left empty — US-MEM-006 adds vector search on top.
3. Token estimation uses 4 chars ≈ 1 token (OpenClaw's approximation). Good enough for chunking; exact tokenization not needed.
4. SQLite DB lives at memory_data/memory.db (co-located with the markdown files it indexes).
5. No external dependencies — Python's sqlite3 module has FTS5 support built in on most platforms. If FTS5 is unavailable (rare), fall back to LIKE queries with a warning.

userStories.title: Improved memory recall prompting and search scope control
userStories.description: As an agent, I want (1) clearer, task-agnostic instructions about when and how to use memory_search, and (2) a scope parameter on memory_search so I can choose to search only the current task, only global memory, or all memory.

existingFiles: memory/store.py (search method — currently searches all files with no scope control)
context.depends: US-MEM-AGT must be done first (all memory tools wired in)

context.reference: OpenClaw system-prompt.ts buildMemorySection() — uses task-agnostic categorical triggers (prior work, decisions, dates, strategies, mistakes) not task-specific ones
context.searchScopeGap: docs/memory-system.md planned a task_id? parameter on memory_search but it was never implemented. Currently search() scans ALL session files (001, 002, 003, ...) + TASK_MEMORY.md + MEMORY.md + daily logs in one call with no agent control.

MemoryStore.search() gains scope parameter that filters which files are scanned
Agent instructions contain a dedicated '## Memory Recall' section (not buried in general instructions)

Memory recall section lists task-agnostic trigger categories (e.g., prior observations, past strategies, known mistakes, previous decisions — NOT game-specific like 'floor numbers' or 'enemy encounters')
Instructions use 'mandatory recall step' framing (not a soft suggestion)
Instructions include failure guidance: what to do when search returns nothing relevant

Level 1: Lint passes (uv run ruff check .)
Level 1: Unit tests pass — add tests for scope='task' and scope='global' filtering
Level 1: Smoke test run_magic_tower.sh 20 doesn't crash
Level 2: After run_magic_tower.sh (step count at discretion), trajectory logs show agent invoked memory_search in at least 3 distinct decision-making contexts (not just once at start)

userStories.notes:
Two parts in one story:

1. **Search scope control**: Currently memory_search scans everything (all session files, TASK_MEMORY.md, MEMORY.md, daily logs) in one call. The agent has no way to narrow the search. Adding a scope parameter lets the agent focus on task-specific or global memory as needed. Default 'all' preserves backward compatibility.

2. **Recall prompting**: Inspired by OpenClaw's system prompt design (buildMemorySection in system-prompt.ts). The current TinyClaw instructions are too vague — 'before making decisions' doesn't give the model enough signal. OpenClaw's categorical triggers (prior work, decisions, dates, strategies, mistakes) are more effective.

Optional enhancement: session-start auto-search — programmatically call memory_search with task-relevant keywords before the first agent step.

userStories.notes:
Evaluation-only story — no production code changes. The goal is to validate the default model choice and document alternatives. The recommended model becomes the new default in MEMORY_COMPACTION_MODEL if it outperforms gpt-4.1-mini.

Candidate models to evaluate:
- gpt-4.1-mini (current default — fast, cheap)
- gpt-4.1 (higher quality, more expensive)
- claude-sonnet-4-20250514 (alternative provider)
- Any reasoning model variants available

Key quality dimensions:
1. Contradiction removal — does the compacted output resolve conflicting observations?
2. Deduplication — are redundant observations merged?
3. Actionability — does the output contain concrete strategies vs vague summaries?
4. Conciseness — is the output compact enough to fit in agent instructions without bloat?
